receipt.public_excerpt: Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) made $974 million from running its business in the second quarter, according to the IPO prospectus it filed Monday. That's operating income

evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic, a leading generative AI lab, reported an operating profit for Q2 2026 in its S-1. That shows it had a path to profitability, against the claim that no generative AI company did.

receipt.public_excerpt: Anthropic reported $11.6 billion in revenue and $974 million in operating profit for the second quarter of 2026, according to its registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on October 26.

evidence_items.explanation: A second report confirms the Q2 2026 operating profit figure from the S-1.

evidence_items.publisher: Gamma (press release via Venture Capital Access Online)

receipt.public_excerpt: The company has been profitable for over two years and scaled to $100 million in ARR with only $23 million in initial funding and a lean 50-person team.

evidence_items.explanation: Gamma is an AI-native presentation company. Seven weeks before the post, it said it had been profitable for over two years. A company that is already profitable has a path to profitability.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Why the $80 billion loss is mostly on paper', paragraph 2

receipt.public_excerpt: Over the full six months, the operating loss was $693 million, because the first quarter's loss outweighed the second quarter's profit.

evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic still lost money over the first half of 2026 and booked a large net loss. This limits how far one profitable quarter proves lasting profitability.

unresolved_gaps: The S-1 on sec.gov returned 403, so the Anthropic figures come from news reports of the filing, not the filing itself.
Gamma's profit figures are company-stated and unaudited. The press release gives no amounts.
One quarter of operating profit does not show that Anthropic's profitability will last, given its large compute commitments.
